source_text.docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolv: Step 4's test must be shown to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the post-fix code. When the pre-fix failure is "the code under test does not exist": the fail-then-pass rule is trivially satisfiable when the fix adds a module (pre-fix failure is UndefinedFunctionError for every test, proving the module is new but nothing about whether the tests discriminate a correct implementation from a wrong one). So: where the pre-fix failure is non-existence, the fail-first requirement is satisfied ONLY by additionally MUTATING the shipped logic and recording which tests fail for each mutant. The mutants must target the specific traps the fix exists to handle, not arbitrary breakage. A mutant is a TEMPORARY PROBE -- leaving one in the tree is a step failure. Preferred: apply mutants in a throwaway git worktree of the branch so the working checkout is never mutated at all; remove the worktree when done. Or, if applied in place, revert with git checkout -- <path> and VERIFY the revert (git status --porcelain lib/ test/ empty, and the test file re-runs green) before completing the handoff.

task.description: Write the regression test for ISS-0276's fix (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.seed.ex, a brand-new module). This is the 'code under test does not exist pre-fix' case named in context.source_text -- satisfy the fail-then-pass rule via mutation testing, not merely by observing UndefinedFunctionError. Write test/mix/tasks/letflow.seed_test.exs covering: (1) running the task against a freshly-migrated empty DB creates a tenant row with idp_realm_id='bpm-default' (ISS-0276 AC1); (2) after running it, Letflow.Identity.resolve_tenant_by_realm('bpm-default') succeeds and returns a tenant whose realm/aud a token-bearing request could resolve past AuthPipeline's tenant-resolution step (ISS-0276 AC2 -- test at the level resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 and the returned tenant's fields, not a full HTTP+Keycloak round trip unless one is already feasible in this suite's existing patterns); (3) idempotency -- running the task twice does not crash and results in exactly one bpm-default tenant. Then MUTATE lib/mix/tasks/letflow.seed.ex in at least 2 ways that target the specific traps this fix exists to handle (e.g. omit idp_realm_id from the attrs map; break the idempotency fallback so a second run raises/duplicates) and record, per mutant, which of your new tests fail -- proving the tests are sensitive to the fix's real logic, not just its existence. Prefer a throwaway git worktree for the mutation so the working checkout is never mutated; if mutating in place, you MUST revert with git checkout -- and verify (git status --porcelain lib/ test/ empty, tests re-run green) before completing this handoff.
acceptance_criteria: test/mix/tasks/letflow.seed_test.exs covers ISS-0276's 3 acceptance criteria (seed creates the row; resolve_tenant_by_realm succeeds post-seed; documented -- doc coverage may simply cite Step 3's README change, no test needed for prose)

At least 2 distinct mutants applied to lib/mix/tasks/letflow.seed.ex, each targeting a real trap the fix handles (not arbitrary syntax breakage), with per-mutant fail counts recorded in result.summary
Post-fix (unmutated) run of the new test file is 100% green, with real command output quoted
If mutated in place: git status --porcelain lib/ test/ is empty and the test file re-runs green AFTER the revert, both confirmed and quoted in result.summary
Do NOT run the full suite or diagnose other issues -- scope is this one test file
